clue.text: Balls covering he'd operated on — about as up-to-date as you can get

definitions.text: about as up-to-date as you can get

indicators.note: to cover is to go over and around, so the word for balls encloses the rearranged letters

parts.note: balls is British slang for nonsense, as is rot

indicators.note: something operated on is cut about and rearranged, so the word's letters move

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Testicles shielding a man who has had surgery, then a remark about being right up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' surfaces as testicles but means rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot news is the very latest, fresh as can be, so it is as current as anything gets.

clue.text: Sex is head from dwarf having tendency to fart?

indicators.note: taking the head from a word removes its first letter

parts.note: Grumpy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White
to pump is British slang for breaking wind, so pumpy is a joke adjective for being prone to it

explanation.surface: A crude claim that sex amounts to oral attention from a flatulent dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word for the second half. Rumpy-pumpy is jokey British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpy-pumpy is a playful colloquial term for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Condoleezza, finally on line, misrepresented what UK and US are supposed to be

definitions.text: what UK and US are supposed to be

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name before it

parts.note: the last letter of Condoleezza
L is the abbreviation for line
to misrepresent the facts is to lie

explanation.surface: Condoleezza Rice, US Secretary of State, finally on the phone, gives a false account of the special relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misrepresented' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym for told untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain and America are formal allies, so they are meant to be in alliance with each other.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Screw a lot, like on the carpet?

parts.note: shag is British slang for having sex
a pile is a large amount

explanation.surface: A suggestion to have sex often, perhaps on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idea of sex on the carpet; in fact it describes the carpet's long, loose tufts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag pile is a thick, long-tufted carpet texture, so it is the sort of thing found on a carpet.

clue.text: Ex-wrinkly given hot tongue

parts.note: a wrinkly is slang for an old person
a flame is a tongue of fire

explanation.surface: A former partner, now aged, gets a hot snog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot tongue' suggests a passionate kiss, but it is a tongue of fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former lover, the same as an ex.

clue.text: Part of your member left inside woman

indicators.note: one letter is placed within the woman's name

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A smutty suggestion of part of a man's organ inside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' surfaces as penis; here it means a limb, the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, so it is part of an arm, a limb or member.

clue.text: Poor Nobby's having to swallow Brenda's condescension

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the Queen's initials
something poor is in bad shape, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the name with its S, apostrophe dropped
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; ER is her royal cipher

explanation.surface: Poor Nobby has to put up with the Queen looking down on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, and ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbery is a patronising sense of superiority, which is what condescension shows.

clue.text: Alex's stuffed — going round the bend about it

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the name's letters wrap the bend's letter
something stuffed is wrecked or done for, so the combined letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the name with its S, apostrophe dropped
a U-bend is shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A man called Alex is fed up and losing his mind over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the old euphemism for sex, so something about it is SEXUAL. The surface 'stuffed' reads as 'done for', which is exactly why it scrambles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Since 'it' is a coy word for intercourse, an adjective meaning concerning intercourse is a fair equivalent of 'about it'.

clue.text: European country snatching Yasir's chief for Palestine

indicators.note: the country snatches one letter in place of one of its own, as the words 'for' make plain

parts.note: the Netherlands, commonly called Holland

indicators.note: a chief is the head, so only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: Yasir Arafat, the Palestinian leader, gives his initial

explanation.surface: A European state takes Yasir Arafat's place as leader of Palestine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y goes in where the second L of HOLLAND was. Arafat, the Palestinian leader, keeps the surface on topic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Land is the traditional Christian name for the biblical region roughly covering Palestine.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Here there are lashings of pop with gin (PS. getting pissed)

indicators.note: a drunk loses order and coherence, so the preceding words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bar where there is plenty of fizzy drink with gin, and the writer adds that they got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashings' surfaces as lots of drink, the British 'lashings of ginger beer'; in the definition it means strokes of the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping post is the pillar a person was tied to for flogging, so it is the place where lashes are given.

clue.text: Limp? It's cunning to internalise supergroup, getting end away

indicators.note: to internalise is to take something inside, so the band sits within the word for cunning

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or crafty

indicators.note: the band's last letter goes away, losing its tail

parts.note: the Swedish pop group, a byword for supergroup

explanation.surface: A smutty question about impotence, answered with a lewd quip about 'getting your end away', British slang for having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting end away' looks like the sexual idiom of the surface, but here it only docks a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flabby is slack and lacking firmness, so it hangs limp.

clue.text: Lunatic pervertedly lays Cyclops on date

indicators.note: pervert originally means to turn about, so the word for lays is turned round

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it there
the setter's pseudonym stands for the first person, I
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A deranged man has his way with the setter on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lays' looks like a sexual verb, but it only means puts. A setter's pseudonym in a clue stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic is used loosely of any idea or act that is foolish, which is what stupid means.

clue.text: Ex-PM Tony Blair extremely protective of chopper (having been snipped)

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on both sides, so the end letters enclose the tool
the extremes of the name are its very first and very last letters

parts.note: the first letter of Tony and the last of Blair

indicators.note: something snipped has been cut short, so the tool loses its final letter

parts.note: a hatchet is a small axe

explanation.surface: Tony Blair guards his manhood after a vasectomy; 'chopper' is British slang for penis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex-PM' looks like it describes Blair, who stepped down in 2007; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was Britain's Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990, so she is a former premier.

clue.text: Naff as a recently done painting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cheap and in poor taste; naff is British slang for this
second meaning: still slightly sticky, as fresh paint is

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second half is a playful description rather than a dictionary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tasteless or shoddy and slightly sticky, like paint not yet dry.

clue.text: Brown's luck, taking tumble on the way up?

definitions.note: A possessive name defining a job title is fair because the 's is read as 'is': the clue says Brown is the answer, which in 2007 he was.

parts.note: chance is luck

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a roll is a tumble

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's fortunes take a knock just as he is rising to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2007 Gordon Brown was Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, about to become PM; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown held the Treasury post for ten years, so Brown is the Chancellor in the clue's own day.

clue.text: House hush-hush Ray's philandering — the doctor reckons being so is too much for him

definitions.text: the doctor reckons being so is too much for him

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: a philanderer strays from partner to partner, so the name's letters stray from their order

parts.note: hush-hush means kept quiet
taken as written; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Gossip that a man called Ray is secretly cheating, with a doctor judging it more than he can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is Dr John Reid, Home Secretary in 2006-07, who called his department 'not fit for purpose' and had it split up; the definition describes the job he found too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic description points at the British cabinet post Dr Reid held and complained was unmanageable in its old form.

clue.text: No stranger to filth, Congress possibly needs escape

parts.note: the House of Representatives is one chamber of the US Congress
to fly is to flee

explanation.surface: Someone used to the police, or to smut, wants to get away from the US legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filth' is British slang for the police, which sends the solver after a criminal; here it means dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseflies breed and feed on rubbish and dung, so dirt is their familiar habitat.

clue.text: Thrust against Dicky and beat it

parts.note: a thrust is a shove
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as is off

explanation.surface: A crude sexual image of thrusting and masturbation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a sly reference to a penis and 'beat it' to masturbation; dicky actually means poorly, and beat it means go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Shove off is an informal command to leave, as is beat it.

clue.text: Snoop hard at it getting stiff

parts.note: someone hard at work is busy
a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: A nosy person caught in the act gets aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' surfaces as an erection; as a noun it is a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a meddler who pries into others' affairs, which is what a snoop does.

clue.text: Some time before Piers Morgan type gets the point — "Retire!"

parts.note: a sec is a short time, a second
Piers Morgan edited British tabloids; ED is the abbreviation for editor
E for east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor finally takes the hint and is told to step down.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union, a sense of retire as in pulling back from a body.

clue.text: Congress coming from behind as party gets hollow majority

parts.note: as and so both mean in that way
a do is a party

indicators.note: a hollow thing has nothing in the middle, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of majority

explanation.surface: A political comeback: a party wins a majority with nothing behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature, as it does in 15 Down; here it means sexual intercourse, a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodomy is anal intercourse, which the definition describes as sexual congress from the rear.

clue.text: Wandering hands encircling one's sweet puffy thing

indicators.note: to encircle is to go all round, so the jumbled letters enclose the number
wandering things stray from their place, so these letters move about

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Groping hands wrapped round someone's soft, sweet bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish' alone is common shorthand for a Danish pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish pastry is a sweet, flaky, puffed-up pastry, often with fruit or icing.

clue.text: One on the job, casually starts to lick erotically, giving a bit of head

parts.note: a temp is a casual worker on a short placement

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A sex worker on duty describes an act of oral sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the job' is British slang for having sex, and 'giving head' for oral sex; the definition is just a part of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple is the flat area at each side of the forehead, so it is one part of the head.

clue.text: (see 10ac.)
Being a peer is miserable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a peer here is one who pees, so being one is urinating

explanation.surface: A lament that life in the House of Lords is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord; read it as one who pees. Miserable here means pitifully small, as in a miserable sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Piddling is slang for urinating and also means trivial or paltry, matching each half.

clue.text: (see 4dn.)
Bill screwed without fuss, messily, Joy in every part

indicators.note: something screwed up is ruined and disordered, so the name is jumbled
a mess has no order, so the word beside it is jumbled too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bill has sex with no fuss, untidily, and Joy is involved throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'with' plus 'out': the two scrambled words are simply put together. Joy looks like a woman's name but is the common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of bliss, so joy fills every part of it.

clue.text: "Wet" hugging Maggie's no.2, getting "one a certain shade of red"

definitions.text: one a certain shade of red

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap around, so the word for wet surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: wet means damp

indicators.note: number two picks out the second letter of the name

parts.note: the second letter of Maggie

explanation.surface: A Thatcher-era 'wet', a moderate Tory, cosies up to her deputy and turns communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' were the moderate Tories Margaret Thatcher despised, which makes the quotes misleading; here it simply means damp. Red is a byword for communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist follows Mao Zedong's brand of communism, one particular variety of political red.
